note: Original descriptions of each aspect in each position, written as observable behaviour. Keys are the aspect letter followed by the position number. Revised against published accounts of Afanasyev's theory (0.2.0).

V1.summary: Knows what they want and acts on it without asking permission.
V1.behaviour: They trust their own drive above anything else and expect to set the direction. Decisions come quickly and stay made, and other people's wishes are something to weigh, not something that steers them. Being overruled feels like a real affront, so they avoid situations where their authority could be tested and lost.
signs: Makes the call in a group without waiting to be asked
Rarely revisits a decision once it's made
Takes being overruled or ignored very badly

V2.behaviour: They can lead and enjoy having a say, but they treat decisions as something to work out with others. They'll give ground on how something is done while holding on to what matters to them, and they enjoy the back-and-forth of it. They readily use their strength to stand up for people who need it.
signs: Enjoys negotiating and finding a deal both sides accept
Changes plans without feeling defeated
Steps in to back someone who's being pushed around

V3.summary: Afraid of humiliation and unsure of their own standing.
V3.behaviour: Pressure feels personal, and being made to look small is what they fear most. They may give in and resent it later, or dig in hard over something small to prove they can't be controlled. They often cover the area with modesty, clowning or self-deprecation, and they take praise and status very seriously.
signs: Agonises over decisions, then defends them fiercely
Jokes at their own expense before anyone else can
Is deeply affected by praise, rank or being passed over

V4.behaviour: They don't need to be in charge and are comfortable following a clear lead. Being told what to do isn't an insult; it often comes as a relief, and they'll agree in advance to a plan someone else makes. Their own wants tend to emerge through other people's plans rather than against them.
signs: Says "whatever you prefer" and means it
Works best with clear direction
Isn't bothered by being called a pushover

L1.summary: Holds firm views and argues to win.
L1.behaviour: They trust reasoning above anything else and present their opinions as settled conclusions. In a disagreement their first move is an argument, and they keep at it until the point is won. They aren't easily talked out of a view and don't go looking for other people's input.
signs: Answers questions with a clear position, not a list of options
Pursues an argument point by point until it's settled
Stays unmoved by arguments they've already considered

L2.summary: Enjoys thinking things through with other people.
L2.behaviour: Ideas are something to explore and test. They're at their best discussing with someone, can see several sides, and will happily update a view when a better argument comes along. They like explaining things and helping others make sense of them.
signs: Likes a good debate for its own sake
Says "good point" and changes their mind
Patiently explains things to people who are struggling

L3.summary: Afraid of looking foolish or being called incompetent.
L3.behaviour: They care a great deal about being thought intelligent and take intellectual criticism hard. They often hide behind scepticism, picking holes in other people's ideas rather than offering their own. Yet they keep coming back to ideas and arguments, and once comfortable they can become surprisingly talkative.
signs: Doubts and questions instead of stating a view
Feels stung when their reasoning is picked apart
Goes quiet among confident talkers, then opens up with people they trust

L4.summary: Relaxed about ideas and happy to borrow other people's.
L4.behaviour: They don't see themselves as a thinker and aren't bothered about it. They use reasoning as a tool when they need it and drop it under pressure. They readily accept an explanation that sounds plausible, and in a discussion they can be loose and playful rather than rigorous.
signs: Defers to someone who seems to know
Isn't offended when called slow or wrong
Takes up a view that sounds reasonable without testing it

E1.summary: Feels strongly and sets the emotional tone.
E1.behaviour: Their feelings are big and clear, and they trust them more than any argument. Their mood spreads to the people around them, and in a disagreement their feelings can carry the day. They don't easily take on other people's moods, and they rarely ask for comfort.
signs: Openly enthusiastic, moved or upset
Others pick up on their mood straight away
Feelings count for more with them than reasons

E2.summary: Emotionally expressive and in tune with others.
E2.behaviour: They feel things vividly and express them with a wide range, matching their response to the moment. They enjoy emotional exchange, shape the mood around them, and are at their best with someone to share feelings with. They offer comfort and sympathy easily.
signs: Picks up and responds to others' moods
Enjoys heartfelt conversations
Is the one people turn to when they're upset

E3.summary: Feels a lot but finds it hard to show.
E3.behaviour: Feelings run deep, but expressing them feels exposed and awkward. They often hide behind dryness or irony and keep a cool surface. Emotional scenes around them are uncomfortable, and they remember for a long time when their feelings were dismissed. With people they trust, or when relaxed, they can be unexpectedly tender.
signs: Deflects with irony when things get emotional
Dislikes being asked how they feel in front of others
Softens noticeably once they feel safe

E4.summary: Easily caught up in other people's moods.
E4.behaviour: They don't give their own feelings much importance and aren't bothered by being called cold or over-emotional. Their mood tends to follow the people around them, and they'll happily let someone more expressive set the tone. In a crisis, feelings switch off and they just get on with things.
signs: Takes on the mood of whoever they're with
Rarely talks about how they feel
Stays practical when things get emotional

F1.summary: Trusts the physical world and their own experience of it.
F1.behaviour: They know what they like in comfort, appearance and possessions, and they arrange their life to suit. They trust what they've seen and done for themselves over anything they're told. They hold on to what's theirs, and in a clash their first reaction is physical: standing their ground and outlasting the other side.
signs: Has a settled way of keeping home, money and things
Believes it when they've tried it themselves
Defends their space and belongings firmly

F2.summary: Enjoys physical activity, comfort and practical work.
F2.behaviour: They like doing things with their hands and body and take pleasure in comfort, objects and surroundings. They work tirelessly and precisely, enjoy testing themselves physically, and adapt easily to new settings. They take practical care of other people as a matter of course.
signs: Throws themselves into hands-on activities
Looks after others' practical needs without being asked
Adapts quickly to a new place or routine

F3.summary: Self-conscious about the physical and material side of life.
F3.behaviour: Comfort, money, possessions, appearance or physical competence feel uncertain. They dread physical confrontation, may be prudish or awkward about the body, and can be quietly envious of people at ease in the physical world. They also push themselves to the limit to prove what they can do, because they don't know where their limits are.
signs: Feels self-conscious doing physical tasks in front of others
Takes on punishing physical challenges to prove themselves
Is hurt by comments about their home, clothes or appearance

F4.summary: Undemanding about comfort and material things.
F4.behaviour: They don't pay much attention to their surroundings, possessions or comfort and are content to let others handle practical arrangements, or to be provided for. They fit in with what a partner wants physically, put up with discomfort without complaint, and lose track of physical upkeep when absorbed in something else.
signs: Doesn't notice or mind a messy or spare setting
Happily lets someone else organise money and practical matters
Forgets physical upkeep when busy
